articles.description:
Funky feudal family frolic Crusader Kings 3 got its second major expansion of the year this week. It's called Silk and Silver (read my impressions), is all about merchant republics, and shipped alongside a beefy free update to the base game which - while largely focused on overhauling economics - also has some funny patch notes and features worth being aware of.
Read more
articles.title: "Abducting your own lover no longer gives you opinion of yourself" declare the notes for Crusader Kings 3's free Florin update, released alongside Silk and Silver

articles.author: James Archer
articles.description:
At this point the tragedy of Driv3r, or Driver 3, or my personal favourite Drive-thrur, is well thumbed. A familiar litany of unrealised ambition, heinous bugs, dull open-world design, and an expensive yet audibly bored voice cast, the accidental comedic highlight of which is Michelle Rodriguez flatly reeling off car theft orders from what sounds like the inside of a Michelle Rodriguez-sized tupperware container.
A more widely forgotten detail is that, for a while, there was a non-zero chance - a belief, even - that Drive Three Er was going to be the opposite. The 2003-2004 hype cycle had sowed the notion that this would in fact be the open-world crime thriller to knock Grand Theft Auto off its perch, and even 22 years before GTA 6's idolising reviews, that was no small promise; Rockstar were still enjoying the balmy success of Vice City, and we could see San Andreas cresting the hill on a stolen, shining BMX. "Ah, but did they have Michael Madsen doing doughnuts in car parks?," publishers Atari asked the world, either unaware or in denial of the spluttering, clapped-out rattletrap they were about to wheel into the showroom.
You likely know the rest, though one of the dangers of familiarity is the subsequent breeding of complacency, which in this case can manifest as a thawing acceptance. I succumbed to this myself, having recently installed a legally unlinkable copy of Drivethreeuh, mind opened to the possibility that maybe it wasn't that bad. Six hours later, I am here to tell you: it was.
Read more
articles.title: I have double-checked and yes, original 'GTA killer' Driv3r really was that rubbish

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
GTA 6 launches on console today. It's widely expected to sell more copies than main character Lucia Caminos has skin pores, more copies than there are words even in Eurogamer's five-star review, which I believe Chris Tapsell has written specifically to exhaust and destroy such neurones as I have remaining. And yet, staff at Rockstar Games are apparently worrying about being laid off, as development winds down and investors start to bicker about Line Going Up Even More.
In an article supporting this month's union vote at Rockstar North, one of the game's animation programmers argues that "workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised."
 Read more
articles.title: "It’s hard not to worry": Even as GTA 6 launches on console amid glowing reviews, Rockstar devs are already concerned about getting laid off

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
In a first substantial update since acquiring SteamDB from its founders back in September, the owners of Nexus Mods have outlined some new additions coming to , the two sides in the deal have announced some additions coming to the community-run backend database. Affiliate links aimed at providing options to help folks find the cheapest price for a game and a new tab dedicated to the mods Nexus host for a game are incoming, as work on behind-the-scenes improvements continues.
Read more
articles.title: SteamDB will add "affiliate links to authorised game retailers" and a new tab dedicated to mods, first update since Nexus Mods takeover confirms

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Goat Simulator and Satisfactory outfit Coffee Stain Group have bought the intellectual property rights and assets for Chronicles: Medieval, the Tom Hardy-garnished strategy RPG that was originally in development at now-bankrupt Raw Power Games. The game will now be made by a new developer, owned 25% by a few former Raw Power devs and 75% by Coffee Stain. Coffee Stain will fund the game's on-going development.
 Read more
articles.title: Chronicles: Medieval devs Raw Power are bankrupt, but their sandbox RPG lives on at a new studio co-founded by Satisfactory devs Coffee Stain

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
As you've probably heard, GTA 6 is out on consoles this week and targeting 30 FPS on that hardware. Despite reports claiming one may not be far away, there's still no official word on a PC port, hence why we've not got a review that delves deep into analysis of just how central to the experience the smell reaction system is.
The wait for confirmation of a PC version continues, then, and it looks like that might well be the only chance people get to play the crime sandbox at 60fps, with Rockstar having confirmed that higher frame rate modes aren't en-route to even the most beefy of consoles.
Read more
articles.title: PC remains GTA 6's last hope for 60fps smoothness as Rockstar confirm such an option isn't coming to even the swankiest consoles

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Freshly published bankruptcy documents for perennially troubled MindsEye developer Build A Rocket Boy have spelled out the scale of the company's debt, with around £61.7 million owed to creditors. The documents also touch on founder Leslie Benzies and CEO Mark Gerhard's claims that MindsEye is the victim of an organised sabotage campaign. The company's leaders have apparently taken out even more loans in order to fund legal action against the suspected perpetrators, with the promise of a healthy payout. I'm not holding my breath.
 Read more
articles.title: Despite being £61.7 million in debt, bankrupt MindsEye devs Build a Rocket Boy are splurging on legal action against "a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews"

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Nvidia's board have indicated that they aren't about to do a big u-turn and reappoint recently resigned CEO Jensen Huang, following his departure after multiple alleged instances of extramarital cavorting were reported by the press. Since his exit last week, Huang has indicated he'd be open to making such a return, were it deemed best for both the company and AMERICA.
Read more
articles.title: Ex-Nvidia boss Jensen Huang offers to return if that's best for the company and America, Nvidia board essentially say 'nah, we're all good'

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
I don't want to write about video games any more, I want to deliver milk in the countryside and hang out with a cow and quirky people! Sorry, what, there's a game all about that called Milki Delivery that came out today? Alright, I'll write about video games again, especially when they look as charming as this one does.
 
Read more
articles.title: Slow down a bit and help a cow find a friend in the lush-looking, hand-drawn, milk deliver-em-up Milki Delivery, which is out now

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
The promise of user-generated content, this idea that you could host a platform that grows infinitely because the people that interact with it make things for it and you don't even have to pay anyone, is an alluring one. And its siren call has come for Dead by Daylight, as developer Behaviour Interactive have outlined the future of the game, which includes a way to make your own bits for the multiplayer horror game.
 
Read more
articles.title: The siren call of user-generated content has caught Dead by Daylight in its snare, as Behaviour Interactive outline a big revamp update slated for next year

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Everything's a bit grim these days, so let's just go all in on the misery shall we? Let's start with this line from the game's Steam page we'll be talking about today: "Mondrayn is a grim JRPG with survival elements where dying doesn't mean the end of your suffering." Crikey! You're telling me the sweet release of death won't be so saccharine after all? Sounds rough, so it's a good thing Mondrayn looks so darn compelling.
 
Read more
articles.title: Mondrayn is a putrid, crunchy pixel art RPG about escaping from limbo where "dying doesn't mean the end of your suffering"

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
I know it, you know it, hell, I'm sure developer Archetype Entertainment know it: Exodus is kind of just Mass Effect again. That's in part because the DNA of the game has been built by series vets like Drew Karpyshyn, Chad Robertson and James Ohlen. But it's also because, well, they're putting FemShep in the game. Yes, I'm being a tad facetious here, but when the latest trailer for your game is literally titled "Female Jun Reveal," well, comparisons will be made!
 
Read more
articles.title: Archetype go all in on the Mass Effect vibes with a FemJun reveal, but I'm just left hoping they'll call the alternative option MascJun to balance it out

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
It's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto. Frankly, it's bizarre to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't GTA 6, which rolls onto console hard drives this week. A decade in the making, with a development team of thousands scattered across an international network of studios, GTA 6 aims to be the Maximum Game. It's both a dense, lively open world and a monument to the exhausting impersonality of "triple-A" game productions. It contains multitudes: birdlife! Realistic cloud formation! Fuel mechanics! Romance! Soda visibly sloshing around in bottles! It's an imperial production shadowed by labour disputes, that appears to have given Rockstar's various teams little time or space to think about anything else.
It wasn't ever thus. Once upon a time, Rockstar weren't just known for GTA and to a considerably lesser extent, Red Dead Redemption. Once upon a time, they had a reputation for slightly dodgy experiments. I recently interviewed former Rockstar North tech director Obbe Vermeij about a few of them, including Agent, the unofficial James Bond game Rockstar toyed with before putting all chips on Grand Theft Auto 5.
 Read more
articles.title: What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Upsettingly, it is that time of the week again, as Take-Two are laying off staff at Firaxis, the developer behind Civilization and XCOM, only a little over a year the last time the studio suffered from layoffs. Firaxis are, notably, owned by Take-Two, the publisher of GTA 6 which comes out in, oh, two days time? Interesting timing, 'ey.
 
Read more
articles.title: Only two days out from GTA 6, its publisher Take-Two lay off staff at XCOM and Civilization developer Firaxis

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
It's a joyous day for lawyers representing plucky little game and console makers Sony. A UK class action lawsuit which accused the company of using the PlayStation Store's dominant market position to fuel "excessive and unfair" prices for digital games has been dismissed in its entirety by the Competition Appeal Tribunal in London.
Read more
articles.title: Sony defeat $2.6 billion UK class action lawsuit which argued PlayStation's dominant market position fuels "excessive and unfair" game prices

articles.author: Ashley Schofield
articles.description:
Update 18/11: Crystal Dynamics have provided the following statement to RPS, confirming it cut eight staff members:
The original article continues below.
As initially reported by Vertical Slice (thanks, Chris!), the workforce of Tomb Raider studio Crystal Dynamics is being cut as part of a new set of layoffs by owners Embracer. As far as is currently known, those affected include senior game designer Joshua Mitchell, senior environment technical artist Kevin Baker, and UI software engineer Garin R. K. Richards, all of whom shared news of their redunancies on LinkedIn. There may be more affected, but neither Crystal Dynamics nor Embracer have offered comments on the reduction of staff as yet.
Read more
articles.title: Embracer begin yet another round of layoffs at Crystal Dynamics, while they're still midway through development on two Tomb Raider games

articles.author: Ashley Schofield
articles.description:
Gloomwood, the Victorian survival horror immersive sim (or, wait, I'm getting reports that we shouldn't call it an immersive sim, apparently) by Dillon Rogers is a game that is quite happily inspired by its predecessors such as Thief, Resident Evil and Dishonored; you could call it 'Thief with guns', if you really wanted to. (Sorry, I've just seen that the domain for Gloomwood's site used to be 'residenthievil.com'. Wonderful). Now, that last inspiration has come full circle, as publisher New Blood Interactive's latest update post confirms that the newest member of the team is none other than former Dishonored designer Julien Eveillé.
Read more
articles.title: Former Dishonored designer joins the team on New Blood's Victorian immersive sim Gloomwood, with a new level and new weapons coming this year

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
For absolutely no reason whatsoever, I’ve recently fired Sleeping Dogs up again. The United Front Games-developed, Square Enix-published open-world crime romp is still as good as it’s always been, and still occupies its own corner in the dingy bar where the GTAs and GTA-likes hang out. Back in 2015, RPS co-founderman Alec Meer (RPS in peace) referred to it as “the halfway house between GTA's sneering arrogance and Saints Row's chaotic nonchalance”. Fair enough, I’ve never been that big a Saints Row guy, but I see slumbering canines a bit differently.
Read more
articles.title: I'm not saying Sleeping Dogs is the world's best life of crime sim, but no other game has replicated the importance of pork buns to whole manhood as deftly

articles.author: Ashley Schofield
articles.description:
As part of a summit meeting in Manchester yesterday, the IWGB Game Workers union have joined up with other unions spanning the Republic of Ireland's GWUI, Germany's GDRT, Italy's FIOM-CGIL, France's STJV, and Spain's CSVI to publish a manifesto that aims to "bring to light the risks and dangers genAI poses to the workforce" for consumers, workers and publishers alike.
The manifesto states that "GenAI is currently harming the games industry, its workers and the games they produce," and suggests actions that can be taken by all to reduce harm done to the industry. The manifesto specifies the "severe harm to the environment, the destruction of communities and the exploitation of the Global South" as wider harms of the technology, but maintains its focus on the industry itself.
Read more
articles.title: "Games are best made by people": The IWGB and other European unions publish joint manifesto calling on workers, employers and consumers to reject genAI

articles.author: Ashley Schofield
articles.description:
Unity's next venture, amidst rumours of it being bought out by the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund, is the Unity Fellowship, a grant program that offers $50k in cash to Unity-using indie devs that plan release a game within a year - without asking for recoup, revenue share, creative control or IP ownership in exchange. I don't need to tell you that all sounds too good to be true, even with the Unity engine requirement, but in fairness, the company has form for handing out cash. The Unity for Humanity grant, just earlier this year, spread $600K across ten different indie projects focused on societal and environmental issues.
Read more
articles.title: Unity launches new Fellowship program, offering a "no recoup" $50,000 grant to indie developers planning to launch their game in the next 12 months

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
It's amazing what a difference a few lines of preamble can make to your understanding of a game. Out now on PC, Steel Gullet is a factory engineering puzzler that, while notable for its meticulous interest in thermodynamics, broadly compares to the foundational work of Zachtronics, together with more recent and focussed conveyor belt wranglers such as Modulus. Resources come in, and you arrange machines on a grid to transform them into something else, before sliding them into an output hopper.


The difference is that you're doing this inside a huge walking fortress city, which stamps across the surface of a largely unseen, devastated and uninhabitable Earth. Your resources are the refuse of a bygone human civilisation: knots of concrete and rebar, flaccid rubber hose and splintered plank, that must be separated out before you can manufacture anything.
 
Read more
articles.title: Break up and re-commodify a fallen Earth in Steel Gullet, a satisfyingly funereal factory puzzler that really loves thermodynamics

articles.author: Ashley Schofield
articles.description:
Split-screen multiplayer is often treated by developers as a forgotten vestige of a bygone age, something to be left behind as the standardisation of online play makes it redundant, especially following the pandemic. It's considered unlikely that you'll have another human being in your home to pick up a controller with you, and since you've inevitably got an internet connection, why not just use that to connect to anyone in the world? I find there's a unique beauty in playing something shoulder to shoulder on a couch with another person, and it seems Fuse Games sees that light too, with Star Wars: Galactic Racer set to be updated to add local splitscreen multiplayer sometime early next year.
Read more
articles.title: Star Wars Galactic Racer will get local split-screen multiplayer in early 2027 with new 'Free Play' mode, finally letting racers yell at one another in a tangible space

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
A judge has denied a motion to dismiss a US lawsuit against chip makers Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron. The suit acccuses the companies of fixing RAM prices and supply, thereby contributing to worsening the effects of the ongoing memory crisis.
Read more
articles.title: Judge denies motion to dismiss lawsuit accusing Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron of worsening RAM crisis by fixing memory prices and supply

articles.author: J.D. Harlock
articles.description:
PC players have been conditioned for decades to accept the keyboard-and-mouse setup for RTS games. One hand has to handle movement and commands through a keyboard, while the other points, drags, and selects with a mouse. Peripheral makers have, usually with the addition of more buttons, made many minor variations to this time-honored arrangement, but there's only ever been one real attempt to rethink it entirely for the PC: the Microsoft SideWinder Strategic Commander.
Read more
articles.title: Microsoft's SideWinder Strategic Commander was a failed attempt to reimagine RTS controls. 23 years later, why are some players still using it?

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
New multiplayer game Spirit Crossing offers up a visually blissful, but inwardly draconian world in which other people are not allowed to talk to you – indeed, not permitted access to the visible electromagnetic spectrum – unless you have given them a high five. By default, players appear to each other as shadows, all exploring a skybound landscape of magic animals and layer-cake mountains that reminds me of both Sable and The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom.


Deign to slap somebody's hand, and they'll pop into colour and be able to join you for various activities. For example, going fishing, playing instruments round the campfire, playing dress-up and pulling emotes in group photos, bouncing around on strangely inflated yaks, or questing forth to heal troubled spirits. There's some material gathering and crafting, and there are recurring storms that make the ambience more threatening, but overcoming a challenge doesn't feel like the point of Spirit Crossing. The "missions" are just an excuse to hang out together.
 
Read more
articles.title: Spirit Crossing, the new Zelda-ish hangout MMO from the creators of Cozy Grove, understands that sometimes you just want to be alone

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
The tentacles of my trade empire snake up towards France in the west, down towards Africa in the south, and off into Hungary in the east. Yet, I still can’t reach out and grasp the throne that sits right in front of me. I’m Marco Sanudo, and the throne of the serene republic of Venice eludes me.
I’ve shed blood in its name, the blood of someone else named Marco no less. I’ve managed to avoid punishment for that crime, despite the fact it earned me a fiefdom to rule while I’ve tried to up my patrician score enough to be the lucky party the next time a ruling Doge dies in office (or runs out their 10 year term). Sadly, Doge Leonardo, the mysterious masked lord who’s had an iron grip on power since the first couple of old blokes to hold the position in this playthrough popped their clogs, is proving incredibly tough to oust.
Read more
articles.title: My murderous wine merchant whines for a chance at republican rule in Crusader Kings 3’s Silk and Silver expansion, which isn't only about the money

articles.author: Julian Benson
articles.description:
This week sees the release of Grand Theft Auto 6, the open-world crime 'em up that's been in development for at least eight years and has been waited on by fans for even longer. Naturally, over on PC we're still waiting for a port to be announced, let alone a release date to circle in our calendars. But, as happens whenever a new GTA is on the horizon, I think about Mafia: City of Lost Heaven.
Released less than a year after Grand Theft Auto 3, Mafia is perhaps a more prescient example of Rockstar's future than their own.
Read more
articles.title: Each new GTA moves the series closer and closer to the original Mafia, the open-world game that bettered Rockstar

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Tech giant Intel are being taken to court for allegedly "misleading" their investors about the sheer scale of the impact of generative AI-fuelled component price hikes on PC sales. The class action lawsuit in question claims that Intel's distribution and manufacturing partners have had to deal with "a massive glut of unwanted PC inventory", and that the gains from Intel's investments in AI datacenters aren't enough to make up for slowing sales of PCs to regular Josephines who just want fancy boxes they can play Deadlock on.
All this follows Intel's last round of quarterly results, in which they announced a significant revenue fall; this triggered an Intel stock price drop from $92.07 per share on October 29th to $65.76 per share the next day, which this week's lawsuit characterises as "the largest single-day price decline for Intel common stock in over 50 years".
 Read more
articles.title: Intel are being sued for "misleading" investors about "a massive glut of unwanted PC inventory" thanks to AI-fuelled price hikes

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
A hacker has pleaded guilty to a number of online crimes, including the 2022 breach of Rockstar Games which resulted in a bunch of mid-development clips of GTA 6 in action leaking onto the net.
Read more
articles.title: GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty to 2022 Rockstar Games breach which the company claim cost them $5 million

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Happy this week, all! Please throw yourself upon the floor in consternation, clawing at your face and hair, for the release of Grand Theft Auto 6 is nigh. In just a few short days, every gaming vertical under the sun will be publishing features about the exact depth of Jason Duval's ripped abs and what this Says About America Today, or how many bottle caps you must gather to unlock Lucia Caminos' Gundam mode.
Fortunately for my sanity, Rockstar's crime colossus isn't yet nigh on PC, though the word is that modders driven nuts by Claude will soon be along with an unofficial "port". As such, while we do have a few Grandiosely Thievish articles in store this week – not least, coverage of the on-going unionisation situation at Rockstar – we can afford to spend a few hours writing about non-GTA things. The appraisal of mushrooms, for example, or the solubility of rubber hosing, or the parrying of spells. Without further ado, here's this week's uncommonly flavourful crop of new PC games. Don't worry, dear Maw. You'll get to eat Jason eventually.
 Read more
articles.title: This week in PC games: start a new life in Vice City, escape a dying universe before the last black hole evaporates, and avenge your pigeon with a sledgehammer

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
"Nobody was hurt" in a shooting last week near the California office of Clockwork Revolution developers InXile, both the studio and local police have confirmed. The incident, which took place on November 11th, is currently being investigated and police have reportedly taken a suspect into custody.
Read more
articles.title: "Nobody was hurt" in shooting near Clockwork Revolution devs InXile Entertainment's office, the Xbox-owned studio and police confirm

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
After a couple of years of regular testing behind closed doors, Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP is now out in open beta, giving anyone who fancies a bit of multi-merc action a chance to give it a go. Though, if you do, be prepared for bugs and crashes, as work on the mod is far from over with the release of this "true beta".
Read more
articles.title: "We've finally reached this milestone": Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP kicks off open beta after around six years preparing for cybermayhem

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
While following a peculiar trail of silver and saffron leaves around the largest roots of the Treehouse, you come across a hexagonal wooden door lying half-hidden among ivy and moss. Scraping away the dirt, you discover a faint, absurd engraving of a newspaper. What mystery is here? You turn the brass knob – strange, it is warm! – and the engraving of the newspaper flutters. The pages turn faster and faster, emitting a howling gale that bowls you head over foot. When you pick yourself up, you are inside a vast attic full of books and bricabrac, lit from one side by windows that offer no view of the outside world – just light and mist.
Tarnation! You have been lured into the eternal prison of Sunday Afternoon. Fortunately, there are several ways to escape. Each of the arcane objects before you is secretly a portal, transporting you to another site of arcane activity, in a bizarre web of diversions that cannot possibly reflect the hand of a human curator. Which will you choose?
 Read more
articles.title: The Sunday Papers

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
If a game is about cooking, at minimum I'll have to give it a quick testspin. Outside of this whole writing about video games thing, my other lot in life is soul bound to food, so I'm always curious to see how the two can be mixed together. And earlier this week, The Snackbar at the End of the World was revealed, a wonderfully cartoonish action-adventure game set in a magical, slightly post-apocalyptic version of 1960s Italy where you go out and forage for ingredients while fending off monstrous crops before turning them into tasty meals back in your struggling restaurant.
 
Read more
articles.title: Forage and fight for ingredients in a magical 1960s Italy and whip up some tasty meals Cooking Mama style in The Snackbar at the End of the World

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
The idea of Dark Souls PvP has always scared me a tad. You can replace Dark Souls with Bloodborne or Elden Ring, I've typically just been a coward when it comes to the idea of fighting another, real person. They're probably going to be better than me! I don't use tactics in Souls games, I use brute force until I get my way! That being said, I do have to admit I quite like the look of Rasen, a game that is essentially just the PvP component of Dark Souls (or PvE if you just want to take on some computer-controlled enemies) that just launched into early access.
 
Read more
articles.title: Rasen, out in early access now, is a PvP focused take on Dark Souls that borrows one of fighting games' best techy tricks

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
When you think about GTA as a series, the first thing that probably comes to mind is driving through crowds of people, gunning down whoever you like, just generally doing crime without any care in the world. I wouldn't exactly call it an empathy game, not to say that other games are any better at such a thing anyway. But with GTA 6 out, crikey, next bloody week, a new interview has gone up with co-studio head Rob Nelson where he shared that you have a bit more space to be empathetic compared to previous entries.
 
Read more
articles.title: Congratulations to people who feel mean shooting random NPCs, because GTA 6 tries "to provide mechanisms that encourage" empathy

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Earlier this year in a bit of a shakeup for the fleshiest kid in town, Super Meat Boy entered into a new dimension in the aptly named Super Meat Boy 3D. I've not played it but it seems like a good take on the format. Clearly, though, sometimes you just need to play the hits, as a new release of the original game is on the way in the form of Super Meat Boy Again+, a remaster with updated graphics, levels and plenty more.
 
Read more
articles.title: From 2D to 3D and back to 2D again, the original platforming classic Super Meat Boy returns with a slick remaster complete with new levels and too many old saws

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
A big part of the point of The Blood of Dawnwalker is that you're on a fixed time limit. You've got 30 in-game days and nights to try and save your family, and if you don't manage to see everything the game has to offer, well, the game's director is fine with that. But that doesn't matter as much now, as The Blood of Dawnwalker is getting its 1.2 update next week that adds in a new game plus mode.
 
Read more
articles.title: Missed something on your first go around The Blood of Dawnwalker? I've got good news, as next week's update adds in new game plus

articles.author: Julian Benson
articles.description:
Ah, yes, Saturday. Traditionally a day for relaxing. Why is it then I'm packing, doing last-minute shopping, and going to a wedding all in the space of eight hours? Because, Julian, you are a fool who, as ever, has left everything far too late.
What about the team, though. I imagine they've managed their time much better.
Read more
articles.title: What are we all playing this weekend?

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Mucky and disreputable kiosk game Probably Stolen – Cyberpunk Shopkeeper Sim is getting three big updates over the next few months that add extra starting scenarios, building on the existing wealth of goods, materials, vocations and techs. Those starting scenarios range from peddling human meat to running the finest cyber-frappucino stall this side of Tannhäuser Gate. There are no hard release dates, and the contents of each update may alter, but developers Questing Goose Studio have shared some rough timeframes.
 
Read more
articles.title: Cyberpunk trading sim Probably Stolen is getting three big updates with new starting scenarios - organ trading, junk empires and fine dining

articles.author: James Archer
articles.description:
Declaring a Best Way of Doing Things is a fool’s game, though in recent years my favourite entries in the Tricky Hitting genre – inclusive of soulslikes and their hybridised disciples – have been the big, bulging ones. Elden Rings and Silksongs, with vast kingdoms and deep, rattling toolkits for surviving them. The reason it’s a fool’s game is because you can also have something like Death’s Door, a taut, compact, lighthearted little actioner that fills eight hours instead of 80 and yet never feels underwhelming or compromised for it.
Read more
articles.title: While soulslikes went bigger than big, Death's Door swung open the appeal of a tighter adventure

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
What's the best prank you ever pulled on a teacher in school, assuming you went to school? By which I mean, a genuinely funny prank that didn't cause any injuries, break any of the more important laws (legal or ethical), or leave anybody with years of mental distress.
I'll start: I once had to write a four-page punishment essay with the topic "silence is golden", after being caught talking in class. I took the essay very seriously for the first three pages, only to end it with the phrase "...but not as golden as my arse." The teacher who set me the essay smugly tore it up without reading it - as I knew he would. Checkmate, Mr Thompson. Decades later, the last laugh remains mine.
 
Read more
articles.title: Worst Class Ever takes asymmetrical multiplayer back to school, with a teacher player trying to spot the naughty children among the NPCs

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Paradox Interactive, publishers of umpteen strategy genre stalwarts including Crusader Kings, Europa Universalis, and Hearts of Iron, have announced plans to switch overlords early next year. Fredrik Wester will make way for Mattias Lilja, as the deputy CEO takes the throne.
Read more
articles.title: Crusader Kings publishers Paradox announce CEO swap, say they're "in a strong position at a time when much of the industry is facing major challenges"

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Much like the H.P. Lovecraft novella it alternately riffs on and skewers, Penguin Colony takes you to an ancient alien city of crabby cuboid geometry and helical designs – comparable at a glance to Lovecraft's "terraces of every sort of provocative disproportion", but here given strangely everyday, anachronistic-seeming labels, such as "Downtown". Later, you're shown flashes of footage of the streets of Melbourne in Australia - developer Origame Digital's base of operations, and a city built on stolen Wurundjeri Woi-wurrung and Bunurong Boon Wurrung land.


When I first set foot in Downtown, in the unassuming body of a Rockhopper penguin, I thought the broad idea was to satirically redefine modern settlements built by European colonisers as Lovecraftian relics, intrusions from the cosmic beyond. This irony seems most pointed in sections where you steer a group of Māori characters, journeying south to prevent an expedition of German and British Nazi occultists from resurrecting a surviving elder being they call the "one true Aryan king". Playing as one of the Māori voyagers, you witness the cyclopean city as a realm of spectral high rises and square windows, rearing out of a swamp of blood and bone.
 
Read more
articles.title: How Origame Digital are channelling and defacing Lovecraft over a trilogy of "inherently indigenous" anti-fascist games

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Microsoft 365 isn't quite living up to its name this week, as its services have suffered an extended outage that's knocked the likes of Outlook, Teams, and Copilot for six. As of writing, the company are finally reporting "encouraging recovery progress in Europe" and are busy "addressing the remaining areas of disruption", but that's only after chunks of November 12th and 13th have seen people, businesses, and institutions left unable to use stuff they rely on.
Read more
articles.title: Microsoft suffer system outage affecting Outlook, Teams and Copilot, exec says there's "no indication this is the result of malicious or cyber activity"

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Clicking a random link this morning, I was dazzled by the glare of a thousand laser batteries firing simultaneously. My ears trembled beneath the trundle of a million caterpillar tracks. Balls of ice, bolts of lightning, shipments of rare alloys, and cascades of drop pods went screaming down my nerves and detonated in my frontal cortex, painting starlanes across the inside of my skull. "Oh god, they've finally found us!" I yelled, hiding beneath my desk. "I for one welcome our new galactic overlords!"
But then I realised that I wasn't looking at a live newsfeed, but merely the Steam page for Horu, a real-time 4X strategy game in which you can "command hundreds of thousands of units across land and space", in the summary of developer David "GlassBeaver" Nadaski. There's also a magic system, this being "the spice that makes your enemy's defeat bitter", which is a very genteel way to characterise glaciating a tank formation or conjuring a miniature blackhole.
 Read more
articles.title: Horu is a sci-fi 4X RTS inspired by Star Wars: Empire at War in which spaceships are spellcasters who can summon black holes

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Xbox have confirmed that Wolfenstein 3 is indeed in production at Indiana Jones and the Great Circle devs MachineGames and that Doom makers id Software have started work on their next game after losing a bunch of staff to the mass layoffs across Microsoft's gaming division this year.
"A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations," isn't part of the marketing spiel for either of those games. Instead, it's something Xbox CEO Asha Shama has bellowed amid a rant outlining how she sees the company's future.
Read more
articles.title: Wolfenstein 3 and new id Software game confirmed, as Xbox boss somehow unrelatedly shouts about one person soon wielding "capabilities that once required entire nations"

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Hark! A new Slay the Spire 2 patch is here! Or, well, it is if you're someone who's trying out the beta branches of the game. If you're not, it might be worth trying out, as Mega Crit say this is their biggest patch for the game so far, with "some really impactful bits of content that will require lots of testing before they reach the main branch."
 
Read more
articles.title: Slay the Spire 2's "biggest" beta patch yet adds its first new early access and foolish character, two game modes, and more tweaks than you can shake a stick at

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
I often find it quite dull that the main takeaway far too many people have taken from Dark Souls, aside from thinking that the most interesting thing is its combat, is that it's all so bloomin' grimdark. I'm not saying I need sunshine and rainbows, I'd just like a vibe that's even remotely trying to be different from FromSoftware's seminal work. And so! I am quite pleased to discover MycoRelic, a Soulslike that pits you as a robot that covers its body in mushroom parts that offer elemental powers.
 
Read more
articles.title: Cover your robot body in magical fungus aplenty and galavant across a mystical, Soulslike world in MycoRelic, now out in 1.0

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Is there a character not originally from a video game that has more games than Barbie? Maybe! I don't want to do any maths right now, but there aren't many that could touch her on sheer numbers. She's had all sorts of digital adventures, her games having a huge influence on the world of 'girl games'. As complicatedly gendered that may now be, the significance can't be understated, and as of today you can have a romp through a nice portion of that history in Barbie Rewind, a compilation of almost two decades worth of games all wrapped up in a nice little decorating game.
 
Read more
articles.title: Barbie Rewind, out now, invites you to take a trip down memory lane with a whole bunch of life in plastic classics, and one game that was previously unreleased

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Look at you, you lucky devil, you're being treated to a new Warhammer 40,000: Darktide class next month! This class is called the Sisters Novitiate, a group of wonderfully violent women with a penchant for crossbows, burning people alive and putting a stop to anyone that dares to oppose the God-Emperor. Neato!
 
Read more
articles.title: Warhammer 40,000: Darktide's next class is the Sisters Novitiate, a group who love staking and burning people for the God-Emperor, and its out next month

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
I feel like one thing I only sort of miss from my youth, viewed through the lenses of those rose tinted goggles, is the established intellectual property game that just copies the formula of another, successful game. Obviously there are plenty of genres that are trendy to imitate, but how often do you see something that's just sort of "thing you know slapped on top of game you know?" Perhaps that's a tad mean, but I do genuinely have a fondness for such games, so I'm quite pleased by the announcement of Conan: The Black Pyramid, an action roguelite RPG that so clearly went to Supergiant Games' School of Hades you have to admire the boldness just a little bit.
 
Read more
articles.title: Conan: The Black Pyramid shoves the titular barbarian into a very Hades-inspired action roguelite with the addition of a few other familiar heroes

articles.author: James Archer
articles.description:
Since we're already sharing trailers from non-Geoff awards shows, here's another: a first in-motion look at Lola's Familiars: Prison of Argnoh, a 2D side-scroller and "lite-vania" that sees its shy witch-in-training making her first summonable friends. Then, borrowing their powers to bust out of a dark fantasy oubliette.
Read more
articles.title: Cartoon-styled "lite-vania" Lola's Familiars: Prison of Argnoh will have you springing yourself, and your summoned pals, from magic jail

articles.author: James Archer
articles.description:
My firstest-ever Golden Joystick Awards, which took place last night in London, was marred somewhat by 1) a gin & tonic costing eleven quid and 2) my view of the stage being directly obscured by its own rigging. Nonetheless, I did crane enough to get a good view at the reveal of The Sound of Fury, a musically-minded hack 'n' slash in which a troubled classical musician descends into Hell to save a friend from the Devil.
Read more
articles.title: The hills are alive with The Sound of Fury, a fantasy musical hack 'n' slash about weaponising pianos to fight the Devil

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Nvidia have ripped off the wax strip and are looking for a new CEO. Jensen Huang, he of the reported extramarital affairs with both a suspected Chinese spy and one of his executive underlings at Nvidia has removed his bottom from the great throne of black and green graphics cards.
Read more
articles.title: Nvidia boss Jensen Huang resigns amid scandal surrounding two alleged affairs, interim CEO appointed as search for sexy leather jacket man's successor begins

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Update: Annnnnnnddd he's gone.
Original story follows:
The situation at the highest levels of AI and also some graphics cards if you insist company Nvidia continues to look, well, less than ideal. CEO Jensen Huang, he of the reported extramarital affair with a suspected Chinese spy, now appears to potentially be on the verge of being chucked out of the window of a black and green corporate tower, following a report claiming that he had a second alleged affair with an executive who reports to him.
Read more
articles.title: Nvidia board reportedly prepare to give CEO Jensen Huang the boot, as second alleged affair thrusts him closer to seriously lusty Crusader Kings playthrough territory

articles.author: Jeremy Laird
articles.description:
Hello, good local-time-zone-adjusted afternoon, and let's just say it's been a while. But I come back to you now at the turn of the technological tide. Well, sort of. Sadly I'm not here to predict an end to the ridiculous AI-fuelled chip crisis. That whole mess has a couple of years to run, surely.
Instead I speak of screens, where there is actually some very good news. In short, have you seen how cheap PC gaming monitors are? I mean remarkably, almost stupendously, cheap. I'm talking £60 / $60 for an entry-level 1080p panel with triple-digit refresh rate, sub-£200 / $250 for high-refresh 4K gaming. Heck, even OLED monitors now start with a "2" in both currencies.
Read more
articles.title: Amid soaring PC hardware prices, gaming monitors are getting cheaper and cheaper. Here's why, and what to buy

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
CD Projekt Red have reportedly enlisted Ukrainian AI firm Respeecher to modify voice lines recorded for the Polish version of Geralt of Rivia in The Witcher 3's upcoming Songs of the Past expansion. The move's been made with the permission of Geralt's Polish voice actor, Jacek Rozenek, and is rooted in the studio wanting his new lines to sound similar to the ones he recorded for the original game prior to having a stroke which has altered how he sounds.
Read more
articles.title: "One of those ways where you can use AI ethically": CDPR have modified Geralt's Polish voice in The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past with genAI, due to actor's stroke

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Back in July, Doom developers id Software laid off around a hundred people as part of wider Microsoft blood-letting. Now, a few of those devs have founded a new employee-owned studio, Hidden Horses. Their first project is Danger Pay, a single-player FPS influenced by ancient arcade blaster Smash TV (pictured) and dystopian movies such as deadly gameshow fable The Running Man – itself an influence on Smash TV.
Hidden Horses have 20 id Software alumni on the books, including former lead VFX artist Todd Boyce, principal engine programmer Dustin Land, senior AI and gameplay engineer Daniel Young, producer Andrew Willis, senior technical designer Jordan Turner, principal technical designer Tim Locke, and senior skybox artist Allison Dombek. They're looking to make "the kind of old school shooters that we think people want more of," in Land's words.
 Read more
articles.title: After being laid off by Microsoft, former Doom devs found new Smash TV-influenced FPS studio that isn't "subject to investor demands"

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Minerva Rising is a post-apocalyptic city builder in which your city extends deep underground, divided into levels with their own resources, industries, and communities. You are an artificial intelligence with overall control, but watch out: if you alienate the population of any particular level by, say, forgetting to supply them with oxygen, subversives may rise up and cut your feed, blinding you to their activities. 
I'm keen to know whether it's possible for every level to lose faith in you and hack your cameras, reducing the game to a pile of "SIGNAL NOT FOUND" messages. I'm also imagining turning the feeds back on and discovering that everybody is having a massive orgy. Stupid sexy vault dwellers! You'll go forth and multiply when Deep Thought tells you to, and not a second before.
 Read more
articles.title: Minerva Rising is a Frostpunk-meets-Silo underground city builder in which rebel citizens can hack your camera

articles.author: Luke James
articles.description:
Some may find this hard to believe, given the absolute state of the market today, but if you were building a gaming PC in 1998, the hard part wasn’t finding somewhere that had 3D cards in stock for a reasonable price. It was choosing the right one among a glut of potential, reasonably affordable options.
In 1998, 47 companies were designing or selling PC graphics, driving a market that hit 130 million units and outsold PCs themselves. Just two years later, at the turn of the new millennium, only 15 remained, and not long after that, there were merely two: Nvidia and ATI, nowadays part of AMD.
Read more
articles.title: There were 47 graphics chip makers in 1998. Where did they all go?

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Black Forest Games, developers of the Destroy All Humans! remakes, have spun out of Embracer Group-owned publishers THQ Nordic via a management buyout and announced plans to form a new "developer-driven group" of independent studios. The new group, dubbed Third Signal, will aim to "give teams the independence, resources and creative freedom" to "bring their own ideas to life".

 
Read more
articles.title: "Some of the best games of the last decade came from teams of fifty": Destroy All Humans! remake devs Black Forest Games split from THQ Nordic to launch new indie studio group

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Loot boxes, dark patterns, virtual currencies, subscription services, pay-to-win systems, and many other trappings of diabolical digital serfdom all face extensive regulation under the European Commission's proposed Digital Fairness Act, which has been formally presented to EU member states today. The full draft text of the regulation leaked earlier in the week. If it passes into law - and there's plenty of debate and revision ahead - it'll have big consequences for the developers and publishers of games like Overwatch, Dota 2, and GTA Online.
 Read more
articles.title: Lootboxes, pay-to-win, virtual currencies and other blights unto gaming face heavy regulation as the EU tables new Digital Fairness Act

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Since they released The Outer Worlds 2 around this time last year, the world has rather turned upside down for Obsidian. The studio lost a chunk of staff to Microsoft's mass layoffs and have pivoted to making a new Fallout game as a smaller group shoved underneath Bethesda in Xbox's corporate structure.
Given all that, The Outer Worlds 2's two-part story expansion is likely arriving in vastly different circumstances than those the studio might've imagined when they began sketching out DLC plans. Part one of the expansion, dubbed  Side Effects Guaranteed, is set to release early next month.
Read more
articles.title: The Outer Worlds 2's first story expansion could well be the opening to the series' last hurrah and will have you hunting for a cure to "explosive cell death" in December

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Warning: I'm probably about to make you feel old. Today, November 11th 2026, is the 15th anniversary of Skyrim's release. The first one, before it was re-released on every other platform under the sun. Fittingly, one of its best expansion mods, Beyond Skyrim: Bruma, has gotten a beefy 2.0 update to commemorate the occasion. Though, its creators insist the main driving force behind the update was more a matter of "technical necessity". There are new quests, dungeons, and corners of Skyrim-era Cyrodiil to explore either way.
Read more
articles.title: As The Elder Scrolls 5 turns 15, massive mod Beyond Skyrim: Bruma gets a 2.0 update delivering a new quest, extra dungeons and an "expanded worldspace"

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Content warning for discussion of extreme violence and self-harm.
 Read more
articles.title: Casualties: Unknown is a total pain simulator that makes other survival games seem like massive cowards

articles.author: Julian Benson
articles.description:
In the nearly 30 years since they opened their doors, Relic have been an enormously influential studio. Responsible for lauded RTS series Homeworld, Dawn of War, and Company of Heroes, they also dabbled in other genres with third-person shooter The Outfit and the original Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine. Yet, despite this history, in 2024, when Relic were negotiating their sale from Sega to UK investment firm Emona Capita, CEO Justin Dowdeswell knew the rights to Company of Heroes had to be part of the deal. "Without it we would have been a dead studio," he tells me.
Without naming names Dowdeswell points out that there are "numerous examples" of studios that weren't able to survive on their name alone. Not only did Relic need the ability to make more games in the series that they were known for, but they also needed the income from back catalogue sales a series like Company of Heroes provides.
Read more
articles.title: Keeping hold of Company of Heroes was essential for Relic to leave Sega, Relic CEO says – "Without it we would have been a dead studio"

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Right, today's been miserable thanks to the now hourly discourse we have to all take part in lest we be seen as approving of the current bad thing, how about something that looks simply pleasant? Today's the launch day for Tanuki: Pon's Summer, a delightfully vibrant mail delivery sim/Tony Hawk's Pro Skater but for bikes about restoring a shrine before the end of summer.
 
Read more
articles.title: Sick BMX flips, colourful characters, a whole lot of mail and a charming raccoon dog await you in Tanuki: Pon's Summer, which you can pick up now

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
You know, I'm sure that Sony had every intention of following through on their intention to release 10 live service games by 2026, as they mentioned way back in 2022. Well, as far as an intention that's designed to please shareholders can go, anyway. And now here we are, almost five years on from that comment that continues to haunt them with the news Fairgame$ has been cancelled.
 
Read more
articles.title: Sony have cancelled Fairgame$, once again reminding us that chasing live service big bucks basically never works

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
It's a bit of a time for AI and games at the moment, 'ey? A bad time, obviously, as it's infecting everything from game development, to the modding community, to native PC ports of a remake of a very popular game that I won't link to for fear of a certain company finding out where I live and ending me there and then. And of course, the latter may be a concern for one Rockstar Games and the impending release of GTA 6. But according to Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick, game's publisher, they are currently technically and legally preparing themselves.
 
Read more
articles.title: Ahead of GTA 6 and as concerns over genAI PC ports grow, Take-Two's CEO says they're revving up their "technical defences" and "legal activites" over piracy

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Marathon is getting a lot bigger next month. In September, Bungie outlined their plans for the shooter making some big promises, namely the arrival of a PvE mode, and now they've shown off what you can expect from its next season, Symbiosis.
 
Read more
articles.title: Marathon is becoming a whole new game next month with a roguelite PvE mode, a beta for a very Halo-esque team deathmatch mode, a vibey social space and more

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
If I wasn't so sick of hearing about AI every day of my life at the moment I might have found it funny to hear that one of the biggest peddlers of the poison around Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was caught having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Oh who am I kidding, it is funny! And despite knowing that this won't likely push Nvidia away from AI, I am a bit tickled to hear that the tech company and Huang are on the receiving end of a lawsuit.
 
Read more
articles.title: Nvidia shareholders have filed a lawsuit against the tech company over claims that they were misled regarding CEO Jensen Huang's affair

articles.author: Julian Benson
articles.description:
The Company of Heroes 3's 3.0 update is huge. Touching virtually every part of the three-year-old RTS, the patch notes are longer than, well, my arm isn't a great measure of patch note length. Let's just say the headline features of overhauled VFX and audio don't really cover it. It also comes with new autumn and winter biomes, an updated grand strategy campaign, improvements to unit AI, and a whole host of other changes.
Talking to Relic ahead of the 3.0 update's launch I learned a little more about the scale of work that went on behind the scenes to make it happen, but also a little more about why Relic are still supporting the game three years after it was released and two years after separating from Sega.
Read more
articles.title: Company of Heroes 3 developer admits "it was a lot" to make the 3.0 overhaul patch alongside regular updates, singleplayer DLC, and a whole spinoff game

articles.author: Ashley Schofield
articles.description:
As another addition to the slew of smaller studios being dissolved by their parent companies, Bandai Namco announced in a press release that they are shutting down their subsidiary studio Reflector Entertainment, a Montreal studio responsible for 2024's action-adventure game Unknown 9: Awakening. In its notice, Bandai Namco explains that the reason for the liquidation is due to Reflector not meeting its expectations for "future business plans, necessary additional investment, and the possibility of profitability and business continuation."
Read more
articles.title: Bandai Namco is liquidating Unknown 9: Awakening studio Reflector Entertainment, following multiple previous layoffs since the game's launch

articles.author: Ashley Schofield
articles.description:
In a press release coinciding with Grand Theft Auto VI becoming available for pre-load ahead of its November 19th release date, Rockstar has confirmed that the game "has been fully developed from the ground up to provide the best possible experience for the current generation of consoles, targeting 30 frames per second while pushing both platforms to their absolute limits." Read between the lines, and you can kind of make out the words "...so hope your PCs are up to spec, computer nerds."
Read more
articles.title: In a reveal that might worry eventual PC players glancing at their GPUs, GTA 6 will target 30fps on all consoles

articles.author: Ashley Schofield
articles.description:
In what has come to feel like the dawn of the final day before Grand Theft Auto VI's release, one thing that Rockstar really don't want people to be aware of is the ongoing legal dispute between the Rockstar Games Workers Union and the studio itself following Rockstar's alleged union busting in firing 31 union members last year. Starting on the 12th through to the 26th, recognition of the union will be voted upon by staff to ensure that workers would be given a say over "topics including pay and bonuses, overtime, redundancies, flexible working arrangements, and generative AI policies."
If it passes, the vote would also make the union the largest recognised union in the UK games industry, partly thanks to its partnership with the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain. Now, the global labor union SAG-AFTRA have chimed in to endorse the Workers Union, offering solidarity to the members involved and granting important leverage from a global force.
Read more
articles.title: "A fight for all workers": SAG-AFTRA throw weight behind emerging Rockstar union ahead of its GTA 6 release week vote

articles.author: Ashley Schofield
articles.description:
In a statement posted yesterday, Killing Floor developers Tripwire Interactive have announced that the studio is laying off 36 "talented" internal staff as part of a "workforce reduction". The job cuts come 16 months after the release of Killing Floor 3 (which James didn't care for), and within hours of unrelated yet equally dispiriting redunancies at Skydance Games.
Read more
articles.title: Tripwire Interactive says it's laying off 36 staff in a "necessary" decision, while reassuring that Killing Floor 3 and Maneater 2 are still in active development

articles.author: James Archer
articles.description:
Valve have finally made clear what they've been doing with all that hoovered-up performance data and all those "Framerate Estimator" text strings: a framerate estimator for the Steam Deck. Or, rather, a framerate average-r, as games on the Steam Store are now getting attached graphs – under their existing Steam Deck Compatibility details – that show how many frames-per-secondseses that game has been recording on real players' handhelds, the OLED and original LCD models both.
Read more
articles.title: Steam's new Steam Deck framerate graphs are good news for handheld players, though I wouldn't fully trust the numbers yet

articles.author: Ashley Schofield
articles.description:
A little over a month following the huge, vile, culture-defining (negative) merger between Paramount and Warner Bros. into Skydance, the corporation has confirmed that games division Skydance Games will be facing a round of layoffs, according to a report from Variety.
Read more
articles.title: Skydance Games lay off an undisclosed number of staff in the wake of Paramount-Warner Bros. merger, in latest case of consolidation killing livelihoods

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
The folks behind Nexus Mods have rolled out a new "daily limit" system which ensures modders who upload multiple works in bulk during a single 24 hour period can't take up more than one spot in the tabs dedicated to showing off new mods for different games. Instead, those who chuck up their mods in bulk will see one of their works given a spot, while the rest are neatly filed away behind it, ready to spring out if you click a bit of text indicating that modder's got other fresh works to show off.
Read more
articles.title: Following site-wide discussion on AI use, Nexus Mods add a "daily limit" to the spots in the new mods tab one person can hog via multiple rapid-fire uploads

articles.author: Ashley Schofield
articles.description:
Friendslop du jour Big Walk is the latest in an unfortunately long series of games that have been confirmed to use generative AI in their production, with developers House House clarifying their use of it in a statement to Aftermath (thanks!). House House state that "LLMs were used sparingly by House House to help work through difficult technical challenges and bugs", and that "well under 0.1% of Big Walk’s code had anything to do with this usage", but are quick to note that "generative AI was not used in any other context when making the game."
Read more
articles.title: Big Walk developer House House reveal genAI use in final stretch of development, only revealing it now as "it has become a matter of public interest"

articles.author: Julian Benson
articles.description:
Poema is my pride and joy. She was my first horse and she's a competition winner, but she's reached her potential. She'll never be a show jumper, and that's where the money and prestige are to be found. If I'm ever to grow my horse farm into a nationally renowned equestrian centre, I need the cash to expand and upgrade my facilities. Poema is a hoofstep on the path to that future, but she's not going to be able to take me all the way herself.
For all its hand-drawn aesthetics, Horses of Hoofprint Bay has hard realities like the limits of Poema's future bubbling under its surface. While the game's scripted narrative may be lacking, it's shockingly easy to fill in the gaps with drama worthy of a Jilly Cooper novel.
Read more
articles.title: Don't be fooled by Horses of Hoofprint Bay's hand-drawn art, this stable management game has all the drama of a Jilly Cooper novel

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Oh shit, that's not too far away. Terrifyingly, that last sentence is now a thing I can accurately write about games coming out in January 2027. Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy has just been confirmed as one such game, with the cRPG's heresy investigation set to commence towards the end of the month.
Read more
articles.title: Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy releases in January, leaving not very long to prepare for all the crunchy cRPG choices and secret wars it'll lob your way

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
It is said that King Canute once placed his throne on the shore and commanded the sea not to get his feet wet, thus proving to his flattering courtiers that only God Almighty holds sway over the elements. "But sire!" I would have told him, if I'd been one of the aforesaid lickspittles. "Why not lay down spike strips and park a couple of flamethrowers in the shallows?" I would have said this because I have just been playing Swarmbreaker, a tower defence game that aims to prove there is no fluid body so awe-inspiring that it cannot be machine-gunned into submission.
 Read more
articles.title: Swarmbreaker is an uncommonly mesmerising tower defence game in which enemies "cluster, collide and flow like a fluid"

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: David Ježek)
articles.description: Dny Haswellu jsou asi sečteny, éra dobře vymyšlených AI aplikací si žádá více výkonu. Současně smete nejen mé 13 let staré PC, ale i nenasytné korporáty v čele s Adobe. Čekají nás zajímavá léta.
articles.title: Jak mě AI ve fotografii a Rust vibe coding donutily přejít na nové staré PC

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Jozef Krajčovič)
articles.description: Na prvý pohľad pripomína krátky text nad fotografiou ružomberskej dievčenskej školy zmes číslic, geometrických značiek a nečitateľných písmen. Pohľadnica odoslaná 19. februára 1900 však ukrýva súkromnú správu.
articles.title: Historická kryptológia: šifrovaná pohľadnica z Ružomberka

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Pavel Tišnovský)
articles.description: Dnes si ukážeme způsob interaktivní změny zobrazení textur, včetně volby blendingu. Následně zkombinujeme dvě operace: vykreslení 3D tělesa z trojúhelníků a vykreslení otexturovaných trojúhelníků.
articles.title: Využití textur ve WebGL a OpenGL ES: vykreslení 3D objektu s texturou

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Petr Krčmář)
articles.description: Konference ORS v Karviné se věnovala bezpečnosti v době rychlého nástupu umělé inteligence, zabezpečení ERP, bezpečnosti mobilního bankovnictví a sítím. Proč máme používat AI s rozumem a jaká rizika přináší?
articles.title: AI snižuje čas na reakci, neměli bychom z ní dělat IA, zaznělo na ORS 2026

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Filip Zatloukal)
articles.description: Sonda do světa svobodného softwaru. Dnes nastražíme pasti na útočníky, vytvoříme si makra pro myš a klávesnici, vyzkoušíme odlehčené vykreslovací jádro webového prohlížeče a zorganizujeme si sbírku fotek a videí.
articles.title: Softwarová sklizeň (18. 11. 2026): nasaďte na útočníky honeypot

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Petr Kajzar)
articles.description: Kdykoliv se mluví o technologiích ve výuce, nastává jakési přetahování: na jedné straně nadšení z toho, co všechno algoritmy zvládnou vygenerovat, na straně druhé obava, že technologie učitele zcela nahradí.
articles.title: Jak nechat AI ve vzdělávání pomáhat a neztratit přitom úsudek

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Pavel Tišnovský)
articles.description: Seznámíme se s dalšími vlastnostmi tohoto jazyka. Ukážeme si způsob realizace jednoduchých algoritmů, řekneme si, jak mimozemsky jsou uloženy zdrojové soubory a seznámíme se slovy určenými pro práci s grafikou.
articles.title: FORTH na počítačích Atari: realizace jednoduchých algoritmů

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Petr Kajzar)
articles.description: Doba vendorlocků je (snad) pryč. To zaznělo v úvodu Národního dialogu pro digitalizaci zdravotnictví, který se 19. října konal v pražském hotelu ILF a navázal na zářijové setkání nerdů okolo FHIR v Ostravě.
articles.title: Když spolu zdravotnické systémy mluví: zápisky z Národního dialogu pro digitalizaci

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: CSIRT.CZ)
articles.description: Podrobně se podíváme na kampaň wfx-loot, koukneme se na opravy zranitelností u společností Apple, Microsoft a Cisco, ale také na kritickou zranitelnost v serveru Apache serveru.
articles.title: Postřehy z bezpečnosti: kompromitace desetitisíců účtů na GitHubu

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Filip Zatloukal)
articles.description: Zakladatel distribuce Rocky Linux představil projekt Ginux, nové jádro operačního systému kompatibilní s Linuxem. Pro prostředí MATE vzniká nový waylandový kompozitor Polo, jehož cílem je umožnit přechod na moderní zobrazovací server.
articles.title: Ginux je jádro kompatibilní s Linuxem, Polo je kompozitor pro MATE

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Jan Fikar)
articles.description: Elektrická síť celosvětově kolísá s periodou přesně 60 sekund. Toto kolísání se každým rokem zvětšuje. Doposud nebyla známá příčina a kolísají sítě na všech kontinentech, i když jsou navzájem izolovány. Podle výzkumníků z Německa jsou původcem UPS (uninterruptible power supply), které každou minutu kontrolují baterii.
articles.title: Za kolísání elektrické sítě každých 60 sekund můžou UPS

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Jan Fikar)
articles.description: V OpenJDK 17.0.6 a novějším byla objevena závažná zranitelnost CVE-2026-114938 nazvaná Java4Shell. Jde o chybu v akcelerované funkci pro dekódování Base64. Chyba se projevuje jen na strojích s instrukcemi AVX-512. K poškození paměti dojde, pokud je na vstupu 64 znaků „A“ a pak znak „=“. V OpenJDK 17 je potřeba 128 znaků „A“ a pak znak „=“.
articles.title: Závažná zranitelnost Java4Shell v OpenJDK

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Jan Fikar)
articles.description: Google bude po vývojářích Androidu vyžadovat, aby se zaregistrovali, prokázali platným dokladem a zaplatili poplatek 25 dolarů. Tyto podmínky platí již od září v Brazílii, Indonésii, Singapuru a Thajsku. Celosvětově začnou platit postupně od ledna 2027. Google spolupracuje s aplikačními obchody Google Play, Galaxy Store, Honor, Oppo, Xiaomi, Transsion a Vivo.
articles.title: Google bude vyžadovat registraci vývojářů Androidu od ledna 2027

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Redakce)
articles.description: Docker je dnes technologie, která proces vývoje, testování a provozování softwaru velmi zjednodušuje. Provozujte cokoliv a kdekoliv. Už nečekejte na nastavení svého serveru nebo na aktualizaci nějaké knihovny. Mějte prostředí jako součást vaší aplikace.
articles.title: Naučte se pracovat s Dockerem a kontejnery (školení)

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Mlčící menšina)
articles.description: Článek na webu blogu sdružení APNIC rozebírá okolnosti poskvantových podpisů (PQC) v DNSSEC. Není to jen otázka prosté výměny algoritmů. Velikost podpisů může zásadně změnit způsob, jakým se DNS odpovědi přenášejí, a proto je potřeba řešit i chování resolverů, limity UDP a používání TCP.
articles.title: Výzvy při nasazení postkvantových algoritmů v DNSSEC

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Jan Fikar)
articles.description: Zaměstnanec Anthropicu Felix Rieseberg chtěl vyzkoušet schopnosti nového modelu Claude Fable 5.2 a dal mu jen jeden prompt: vytvořit 3D střílečku v prohlížeči. Fable přemýšlel asi 8 hodin, propálil asi 3 milióny tokenů v ceně zhruba 550 dolarů a vznikl HTML soubor o velikosti jen 1,4 MB.
articles.title: Claude napsal 3D střílečku v 1,4 MB HTML souboru

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Petr Krčmář)
articles.description: Vývojáři uvolnili očekávanou novou verzi databáze PostgreSQL 19. Usnadňuje správu databází s velkou zátěží a přidává funkce pro vývojáře i správce. Podrobně o novinkách psal už na jaře Pavel Stěhule v článku PostgreSQL 19: zmenšení tabulek pomocí REPACK bez obav.
articles.title: PostgreSQL 19 přináší údržbu tabulek bez odstávky a nové možnosti replikace

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Petr Krčmář)
articles.description: Vývojáři uvolnili novou verzi programovacího jazyka PHP 8.6.0, která přináší mimo jiné částečnou aplikaci funkcí, výchozí hodnoty pro vlastnosti readonly a nové možnosti pro práci s I/O.
articles.title: PHP 8.6 zjednodušuje práci s funkcemi a přidává nové API

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: PeRu)
articles.description: Vývojáři PHP vydali bezpečnostní verze PHP 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 a 8.2.36. Opravují 17 zranitelností, z nichž sedm má kritické hodnocení CVSS 9.2. Stejné opravy obsahuje i dnes vydané PHP 8.6.0. Nejvíc pozornosti budí chyba phpAfterShell (CVE-2026-126714) ve výchozím souborovém úložišti session. Když je zapnuté sledování průběhu uploadu ( session.upload_progress.enabled, dosud výchozí), PHP přepisuje soubor session neatomicky ještě při zpracování neautentizovaného multipart požadavku.
articles.title: PHP opravuje sedm kritických chyb, phpAfterShell obchází říjnovou záplatu

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Petr Krčmář)
articles.description: Předběžné stahování hry GTA 6 ukázalo, jak zvládnout mimořádný nápor na internetovou infrastrukturu. Podle článku RIPE Labs si hru předobjednalo přes 12 milionů lidí a její soubory mají dohromady přes 200 GB. Kdyby se všechna data stahovala z jediného serveru, znamenalo by to teoretickou zátěž 2,4 exabajtu.
articles.title: RIPE Atlas změřil, jak se hráčům doručují stovky gigabajtů GTA 6

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Petr Krčmář)
articles.description: Společnost Flipper Devices spustila na Kickstarteru kampaň pro Flipper One, kapesní zařízení zaměřené na práci se sítěmi a linuxové experimenty. Zájem je výrazný: za první den přispěvatelé poslali přes 7,4 milionu eur, tedy zhruba 27násobek původního cíle kampaně, který činil 272 655 eur. Kampaň začala 17. listopadu a potrvá do 17. prosince 2026.
articles.title: Kapesní linuxový počítač Flipper One je na Kickstarteru

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Petr Krčmář)
articles.description: Část vývojářů distribuce Manjaro Linux založila v Německu neziskovou organizaci Manjaro Project e.V. Ta je nezávislá na společnosti Manjaro GmbH & Co KG. Tato změna navazuje na spor o řízení projektu, který letos probíhal mezi několika přispěvateli a Philipem Müllerem, vedoucím projektu a ředitelem společnosti.
articles.title: Manjaro zakládá nezávislou neziskovou organizaci

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: PeRu)
articles.description: Vývojáři Ruby vydali verze 4.0.10, 3.4.13 a 3.3.14, které opravují sedm bezpečnostních chyb v regulárních výrazech a v převodu velikosti písmen. Podle autorů existují funkční ukázky, že některé z nich vedou ke vzdálenému spuštění kódu. Identifikátory CVE zatím přiděleny nejsou, chyby proto mají jen označení GHSA. Čtyři z nich nahlásil Stephan Lipp z Ada Logics spolu s firmou Anthropic.
articles.title: Ruby opravuje sedm chyb, kvůli písmenu ß hrozí vzdálené spuštění kódu

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Petr Krčmář)
articles.description: Drew DeVault oznámil ukončení vývoje projektu Redict, forku databázového systému Redis. Poslední vydanou verzí je Redict 7.3.6. Projekt vznikl po změně licence Redis v roce 2024 a měl nabídnout komunitní alternativu s copyleftovou licencí.
articles.title: Redict končí, jeho autor doporučuje přejít na Valkey

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Petr Krčmář)
articles.description: Provoz uzlem NIX.CZ večer poprvé překonal hranici čtyř terabitů za sekundu. V tomto peeringovém uzlu si poskytovatelé připojení a služeb vzájemně předávají data.
articles.title: NIX.CZ zaznamenal rekordní tok 4 Tbps díky stahování hry GTA 6

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Petr Krčmář)
articles.description: Vývojáři PHP upozornili na kritické bezpečnostní chyby, které se týkají všech podporovaných verzí jazyka. Dnes plánují vydat opravné verze, mezi 15:00 a 15:30 středoevropského času. Podrobnosti o zranitelnostech zatím nebyly zveřejněny, mělo by ale jít o několik problémů, z nichž nejzávažnější dosahuje na kritickou úroveň.
articles.title: PHP dnes vydá bezpečnostní aktualizace pro všechny podporované verze

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: PeRu)
articles.description: Bezpečnostní výzkumníci ze společností Wiz, Rapid7 a dalších týmů odhalili dvě kritické zranitelnosti webového serveru Nginx, označené jako CVE-2026-123633 a CVE-2026-123007. Obě mají hodnocení CVSS 4.0 9,2 a umožňují útočníkovi vzdáleně spustit libovolný kód na serveru bez nutnosti autentizace. Podmínkou zneužití je zapnutý protokol HTTP/2.
articles.title: Nginx má dvě kritické zranitelnosti v modulu HTTP/2 umožňující vzdálené spuštění kódu

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Mlčící menšina)
articles.description: FreeBSD vydalo 17. listopadu celkem 21 bezpečnostních výstrah, od SA-26:74 do SA-26:94. Následující výběr obsahuje nejdůležitější dosud neohlášené problémy.
articles.title: FreeBSD má závažné chyby jádra, Kerberos, IPsec a bsnmpd

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: David Ježek)
articles.description: Vývojáři FreeBSD nadále usilovně pracují na podpoře snadné instalace desktopu s Plasmou „na jedno kliknutí“. Nestihli FreeBSD 15.0 ani 15.1 a nyní už je jasné, že ani verze 15.2 nebude tou vyvolenou. Novým termínem pro toto významné zlepšení pro zájemce o desktopové užívání FreeBSD, je vydání verze 15.3.
articles.title: Snadná instalace desktopu s KDE Plasma až ve FreeBSD 15.3

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: David Ježek)
articles.description: Jsme necelé dva roky od vydání desktopového prostředí Xfce ve verzi 4.20 a verze 4.22 je blízko. Původní plány byly optimističtější, v tuto chvíli to vypadá, že Xfce 4.22 vyjde někdy v příštím roce. Aktuálně se blíží vydání vývojové verze Xfce 4.22pre1, která je v plánu na 15. prosince.
articles.title: Vydání Xfce 4.22 patrně na jaře 2027

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: johny)
articles.description: Spoločnosť Anthropic, ktorá vyvíja jazykové modely Claude, dnes večer stanoví konečnú cenu svojich akcií. Obchodovať sa s nimi má začať na burze Nasdaq pod skratkou ANT vo štvrtok 19. novembra. Anthropic bude prvým z veľkých amerických AI laboratórií, ktoré vstúpi na burzu.
articles.title: Anthropic zajtra vstupuje na burzu

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Netolish)
articles.description: Doména codeberg.org hostující mnoho open-source projektů zmizela dnes 18. listopadu 2026 v 05:52:56.865Z z DNS. Status je client hold. Snad to nebude nic vážného.
articles.title: Doména codeberg.org zmizela z DNS

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Redakce)
articles.description: Jaké jsou postupy organizovaných cyber-crime skupin? Co vše je možné koupit na Darknetu? Jaké informace odtud získat? Jakými prostředky bankomat brání útočníkům, aby se dostal k uloženým penězům? Jde se k těmto penězům dostat bez použití hrubé síly? Lze hacknout auto? Co mobilní telefon? Je pravda, že vás téměř každá tiskárna nenápadně a potají sleduje? Jak kompromitovat uživatelskou stanici? Jak tomu zabránit?
